entity_resolution.arabic_name: أبو علي، الحسن بن الحسن بن الهيثم
alternative_names: Abū ʿAlī al-Ḥasan ibn al-Ḥasan ibn al-Haytham

timeline_a_biological.event: Born in Basra during the Buyid dynasty period of the Abbasid Caliphate.
Feigned madness in Cairo under Caliph Al-Hakim bi-Amr Allah to avoid execution after realizing the Nile damming project was engineeringly impossible with contemporary technology.
Released from house arrest following the death of Caliph Al-Hakim; resumed full-time scientific research near the Al-Azhar Mosque in Cairo.
Died in Cairo, Fatimid Caliphate, leaving behind over 200 treatises on mathematics, optics, physics, and astronomy.

timeline_b_scientific.description: Began drafting the multi-volume masterwork Kitāb al-Manāẓir (Book of Optics) while under house arrest in Cairo.
Completed Kitāb al-Manāẓir, establishing the intromission theory of vision, the camera obscura, and controlled systematic experimentation as the core of scientific methodology.
Formulated and solved Alhazen's Problem regarding reflection from spherical mirrors using the intersection of a circle and a hyperbola.
Authored Treatise on Light (Maqāla fī al-Ḍawʿ) and On the Light of the Moon, proving sunlight is self-luminous while moonlight is reflected light using quantitative optical experiments.

physics_analysis.contribution_name: Intromission Theory of Vision and Rectilinear Light Propagation
physics_analysis.scientific_problem: Resolving the conflict between the mathematical emission theory (Euclid, Ptolemy: visual rays emit from the eye) and the physical intromission theory (Aristotle, Epicurus: forms enter the eye), while establishing the rectilinear motion of light rays.
physics_analysis.hypothesis: Light rays emanate from every point on an illuminated object in straight lines in all directions and enter the eye, where an inverted image is formed at the crystalline lens.
physics_analysis.model_or_framework: Ray Optics, Camera Obscura Model, Controlled Empirical Validation.
physics_analysis.experiment_details: Utilized dark chambers with micro-apertures (camera obscura / al-Bayt al-Muẓlim) exposing light from multiple lamps to screens, demonstrating that light rays move strictly in straight lines without blending or curving.

variables_definition.\\theta_i: Angle of incidence relative to the surface normal
variables_definition.\\theta_r: Angle of reflection relative to the surface normal

equations.validity_domain: Planar, spherical, cylindrical, and parabolic specular reflectors
equations.assumptions: Homogeneous, isotropic media and smooth reflecting surfaces

physics_analysis.result_and_impact: Overthrew the ancient emission theory of vision; established modern geometrical optics and introduced modern scientific experimental control.
physics_analysis.limitations_and_boundary_conditions: Lacked the exact physical mechanism of retinal signal transduction and modern electromagnetic wave theory.

physics_analysis.scientific_problem: Determining geometrically the exact point of reflection on a spherical surface given the positions of a fixed point light source and an observer's eye.
physics_analysis.hypothesis: The point of reflection on a spherical surface can be geometrically constructed by finding the intersection of a circle and an equilateral hyperbola.
physics_analysis.experiment_details: Constructed geometric proofs using conic sections (parabolas and hyperbolas) alongside spherical mirror apparatuses.

variables_definition.\\theta_i: Angle between incoming ray vector from source A to reflection point P and normal vector N at P
variables_definition.\\theta_r: Angle between outgoing ray vector from P to receiver B and normal vector N at P

equations.assumptions: Specular reflection on a smooth spherical surface of radius R in a uniform medium

physics_analysis.result_and_impact: Solved a major open geometric optics problem that remained a benchmark challenge for centuries, later analyzed analytically by Huygens and Barrow.
physics_analysis.limitations_and_boundary_conditions: Limited to geometric/conic constructions before the analytical geometry of Descartes was developed.
